text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Main opposition leader Mesut Yilmaz says the attack in a Budapest hotel against him was organised in Istanbul.
- Former head of national roads administration Atalay Coskunoglu sentenced to three years in jail for corruption.
- International Labour Organisation report says 27 percent of the work force in Turkey is jobless.
- Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller tells the West she has kept promises she gave on democratisation.
- Interpol documents reveal that Abdullah Catli, killed in a car crash where a police chief died and an MP was injured, was a leading member person of drug Mafia.
- Islamist Welfare Party help clear coalition partner Ciller of corruption charges in the second case against her.
- Istanbul stock exchange breaks new record. Index over the 90,000 barrier.
- The trail of policemen charged with killing leftist journalist postponed because of bureaucratic delays.
- Parliament extends emergency rule for another four months in nine provinces in southeast Turkey.
